title: Maximize Return with Partial Investments
real_world_story: A financial planning system allows an investor to divide funds across investment opportunities. Unlike fixed investments, some opportunities can be partially funded, allowing the investor to invest any fraction of the available amount.

real_world_connection.target_represents: Maximum return achievable with the available capital
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Prioritizing investments according to their return per unit of cost and allowing partial investment

problem_statement: Given N investment opportunities, each with a cost and expected return, and a maximum available capital, determine the maximum return that can be achieved when investments can be selected partially.
task: Maximize the expected return by selecting investments based on their return-to-cost ratio. An investment may be partially selected.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and B, representing the number of investments and the available capital. The next N lines contain two integers cost and return for each investment.
output_format: Print the maximum expected return rounded to two decimal places.

examples.explanation: The first two investments use 30 units of capital and provide 160 return. The remaining 20 units are invested in the third opportunity, giving an additional 80 return.
Both investments can be fully selected because their combined cost is exactly 30.

expected_algorithm.name: Fractional Knapsack
expected_algorithm.reason: Investments can be partially selected, so choosing opportunities with the highest return-to-cost ratio first maximizes the total return.

hint: Calculate the return-to-cost ratio for every investment.
Take the highest-ratio investment completely when possible.
If the remaining capital is insufficient, take the required fraction of the next investment.
real_world_takeaway: Fractional Knapsack represents financial allocation situations where available capital can be divided across investment opportunities.
